newsitem.title: UK: BP makes Scottish oil find.
newsitem.headline: BP makes Scottish oil find.

text.p: British Petroleum Co. Plc said Monday it has discovered a third oilfield 100 miles west of the Shetland Islands off the northeast coast of Scotland.
BP and Royal Dutch/Shell Group each own 50 percent of the block.
BP said an exploration well on the Atlantic Margin encountered a "potentially commercial volume of hydrocarbons on UK Block 204/19."
Britain's Department of Trade and Industry welcomed the discovery, announcing it would offer two extra blocks north of the find for licensing.
BP said the well was drilled in 850 meters (yards) of water by the semi-submersible drilling rig Ocean Alliance between April 8 and June 8, 1996.
Although the well was not tested, log and core data confirmed the presence of hydrocarbons, BP said.
BP is expected to bring its first Atlantic Margin field, Foinaven, on stream in April. The second field, Schiehallion, should be producing by mid-1998.

"This is an encouraging discovery. BP and our partner Shell need to carry out further work to establish whether the discovery is commercial," said BP's deputy chief executive of exploration Richard Olver.
